text.p: - Ruling Liberal Democrats came first in Slovenia's second general election on Sunday with 27.1 percent of votes. Final unofficial results show the People's Party received 19.6 percent of the vote, while the Social Democrats were at 16 percent.

- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said he would start negotiations about forming a new coalition this week, immediately after final official results were available. The figures are expected to be released on Friday.
- Officials said only 20 individual complaints were lodged about the election, just a few of which concerned what they called real violations of the electoral procedure.
- Slovenia's exports totalled $700 million in September, 4.8 percent less than in the same month last year, the Statistical Office said.

- Final inoffical results indicate the Liberal Democrats would get 25 seats in the 90-member parliament. The People's Party would get 19 seats, the Social Democrats 16 seats, and Christian Democrats, the Liberal's coalition partner, 10.
- Slovenia's soccer team lost 2-1 against Bosnia in a group one World Cup qualifying match on Sunday, forfeiting all chances to qualify for the Cup's final round.
- Gross average wages fell 0.7 percent in August from July, but were up 5.1 percent compared to the same month of 1995, the government's Institute of Macroeconomic Analyses reported.
- Number of overnight guests in the country's 15 helth resorts fell one percent in the first nine months of the year compared to the same period of 1995.
- Slovenia to participate in World Travel Market, a tourism fair opening in London on Monday.
